justification: Both depict a bearded royal/attendant male in strict left-facing profile with a tall headdress, tightly regimented rows of curled beard and hair falling behind the neck, and a richly textured fringed garment, carved in low relief on a rectangular panel — a very specific shared conventional formula for representing a dignitary. The main difference is scope and detail: A shows the full standing figure holding a vertical spear with a bow slung on the back at small scale with thin incised lines, while B is a large close-up bust with heavy modelled relief, patterned diadem and no visible weapon or hands.
